newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Key aide falls ill in new blow for S.Korea's Kim.
newsitem.headline: Key aide falls ill in new blow for S.Korea's Kim.

text.p: In a further blow to South Korea's beleaguered President Kim Young-sam, one of his closest aides -- tipped as a possible presidential successor -- was in hospital on Wednesday after collapsing.
Choi Hyung-woo, 61, who heads a faction of Kim loyalists within the ruling New Korea Party, collapsed on Tuesday and suffered brain damage, hospital officials said.

Three other leading figures in the so-called "minju" faction are in custody after being charged in a bribes-for-loans scandal involving bankrupt Hanbo Steel Co. The scandal has badly hurt Kim's image by opening his inner circle to corruption charges.
Last month, Kim dumped four top presidential Blue House aides as part of a sweeping administration reshuffle designed to restore his credibility.
Kim also changed his prime minister and reshuffled his cabinet.
Choi was untainted by the Hanbo affair.
He is one of nine ruling party elders -- dubbed the "nine dragons" -- tipped as contenders for the party's nomination as presidential candidate in elections in December.
Choi was also believed to be in line to succeed Lee Hong-koo as party chairman. An announcement on that appointment is expected on Thursday.
With his loyalist ranks thinning, Kim was rapidly running out of options as he mobilised his forces for the final battle of his presidency -- to put in place a successor.
Kim is barred by the constitution from seeking a second term, but political analysts say he will try to work behind the scenes as kingmaker.
Lee kicked off the race for the presidency on Tuesday by declaring his intention to run.
Choi is a six-term member of the National Assembly.
"He was once listed as being in a semi-coma but is recovering," one hospital official said. "He is still unable to speak and we will have to monitor his condition for at least two weeks."
